author: Maxim-Doronin
title: CachingTest LoadMultiWithConfig_race fails - import_model call count mismatch
signature: Actual function call count doesnt match EXPECT_CALL import_model Expected called times Actual called times unsatisfied and active|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: C++ unit tests / C++ unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: CachingTest/CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race/ByModelName_testCache fails: import_model expected 3 times but called once

key_errors:
caching_test.cpp(2667): error: Actual function call count doesn't match EXPECT_CALL(*mockPlugin, import_model(A<std::istream&>(), _))...
  Expected: to be called 3 times
    Actual: called once - unsatisfied and active
root_cause: The test CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race is a race-condition stress test that runs up to ~140 iterations to provoke a concurrent cache import_model call. The test expects import_model to be called exactly 3 times (one per device), but under the current run only 1 call occurred before the 2-second test window expired. This is a timing-sensitive flaky test: if threads don't all compete within the 2-second window, fewer import_model calls are recorded. The failure is not caused by the PR's change (src/plugins/intel_npu/tests/driver_version.json, unrelated to inference/caching), confirming this is a pre-existing test flakiness.
reproduction_steps: Run on Windows CI with reduced system load; run `caching_test.exe --gtest_filter=CachingTest/CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race/ByModelName_testCache` multiple times.
recommended_actions: Re-add PR #37114 to the merge queue - the failure is unrelated to the PR change.
File a known flaky test issue for CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race and add it to the flaky test list.
Consider increasing the race timeout or relaxing the EXPECT_CALL count from exactly 3 to at-least 1.
prevention_strategies: Race-condition tests should use flexible call count expectations (AtLeast(1)) and/or longer timeout windows to avoid CI flakiness.
historical_context: This type of mock call count mismatch in race tests is a common flakiness pattern in Windows CI runners which can be slower/more variable than Linux.
